correctness.rationale: In a rank-two representable matroid, a nonzero projective direction is spanned by sampling its own class or two distinct other classes. Independent Poisson arrivals give a disjoint survival-event decomposition and integrate to E_i=n sum_{j!=i}1/(n-a_j)-(r-2), a strict function of the target multiplicity. This proves exact balance iff positive multiplicities agree, with all-zero-coordinate exclusion. Count occupied directions, labeled multinomials, and (q-1)^n scalar choices; divide by the free GL_2(q) row-space action. Full rank and no-zero denominators checked algebraically. Fixed-q Stirling and exponential largest-eligible-divisor dominance yield the uniform subsequence asymptotic. Independent subset-counting vs exponential expectation and complete prime-field matrix enumerations match the theorem. No finite computational result is treated as a proof for all prime powers.

originality.rationale: The August 20 2026 generalized-random-access paper studies information-coordinate and joint requests, projective geometry, symmetry, MDS/simplex and quasi-arcs, not an exact labeled code-subspace census of coordinate recovery balance. The later October 20 2026 matroid paper gives a general coordinate-recovery expectation and duality, and a prevalence bound among unrestricted sparse-paving matroids, but expressly separates representable matroid counts. The earlier Gruica et al. general formula and Boruchovsky et al. dimension-two request formula can imply the rank-two local expectation identity, so that identity is not novel. A separate indexed rank-two full-message coverage optimum concerns a different objective. Actual mathematical-record searches for equal projective multiplicities, rank-two balanced codes, exact counts, and divisor-dependent rarity did not return this population theorem. value.rationale: The probability of coordinate recovery balance among actual representable codes is a motivated quantitative question, distinct from the probability among arbitrary matroids or a full-message optimum. The theorem yields an exact census for every finite field and length, identifies absent lengths, and exhibits a sharp arithmetic contrast: a polynomially rare subsequence when the number of projective directions divides n, exponentially rare otherwise. These are nontrivial population/scale facts useful as a baseline for higher-rank representable balance, while acknowledging the rank-two structural classification itself is elementary.
